gloss: sasa dango; mugwort rice dumpling wrapped in bamboo leaves

definitions.gloss: sasa dango; mugwort rice dumpling wrapped in bamboo grass leaves
definitions.explanation: A traditional Niigata sweet: a sticky-rice dumpling kneaded with {蓬|よもぎ} (mugwort), filled with sweet bean paste, wrapped in {笹|ささ} (bamboo grass) leaves and steamed. The leaves give a fresh fragrance and serve as a natural preservative.

examples.japanese: ⟦{新潟|にいがた}→新潟：27452_niigata⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{笹団子|ささだんご}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{買|か}った→買う：00489_kau⟧。
examples.english: I bought some Niigata sasa dango.

examples.japanese: {笹団子|ささだんご}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{蓬|よもぎ}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{香|かお}り→香り：00189_kaori⟧がして⟦{美味|おい}しい→美味しい：00740_oishii⟧。
examples.english: Sasa dango has a wonderful mugwort aroma and tastes delicious.

examples.japanese: {笹団子|ささだんご}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{笹|ささ}の{葉|は}→笹の葉：18967_sasanoha⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{解|ほど}いて⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧⟦{食|た}べる→食べる：00396_taberu⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{基本|きほん}→基本：00226_kihon⟧だ。
examples.english: The basic way to eat sasa dango is to unwrap the bamboo leaves before eating.

notes:
A famous regional specialty (⟦{名産|めいさん}→名産：21548_meisan⟧) of Niigata Prefecture. Said to date back to the Warring States era, when it was carried as a portable, long-lasting food. Today widely sold as a souvenir (⟦お{土産|みやげ}→お土産：01353_omiyage⟧).

ETYMOLOGY:
- ⟦{笹|ささ}→笹：04407_sasa⟧: bamboo grass (the wrapping)
- {蓬|よもぎ}: mugwort (kneaded into the dough)
- あんこ: sweet bean paste (the filling)
- The bundle is tied with い{草|ぐさ} or string and steamed.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{柏餅|かしわもち}→柏餅：19485_kashiwamochi⟧: oak-leaf-wrapped rice cake — eaten at Children's Day, different region
- {粽|ちまき}: zongzi-style sticky rice — pyramidal, often savory
- ⟦{草餅|くさもち}→草餅：15810_kusamochi⟧: mugwort rice cake — same flavor as sasa dango but unwrapped
